title: Data brokers
subtitle: Data brokers collect, buy, and sell detailed profiles on you to sell to anyone with a few bucks to spare. This guide walks through how to find and remove your data, and how to stop new data from accumulating.

context.title: The impact on your privacy
context.body: Data brokers build profiles containing hundreds of data points on all of us, sourced from public records, social media, loyalty programs, app usage, and location data. They sell this data to advertisers, insurers, employers, landlords, and government agencies.
context.body2: US government agencies including ICE have been documented purchasing location data directly from brokers to track individuals - bypassing the need for a warrant. Stalkers, doxxers, and scammers also use people-finder sites to locate targets.

warning.body: Realistic expectations: Data broker removal is not a one-time fix. New data gets added continuously and you'll need to repeat opt-outs periodically - roughly every 3-6 months. Even thorough manual removal won't reach every broker. The goal is meaningful reduction, not perfection.

sections.label: What data brokers know about you

items.name: Types of data brokers and what they collect
items.path: Background knowledge - no action required yet
items.why: Data broker profiles can include your full name, current and past addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, relatives' names, estimated income, property records, voting registration, criminal records, social media profiles, browsing history, purchase history, and precise location data.

steps.text: `People-finder sites` (Spokeo, BeenVerified, Whitepages) - sell your address, relatives, and phone number to anyone
`Marketing brokers` (Acxiom, Experian Marketing) - sell demographic and behavioral profiles to advertisers
`Location data brokers` (Gravy Analytics, Venntel) - sell precise GPS movement data collected from apps
`Background check sites` (Instant Checkmate, TruthFinder) - sell criminal, employment, and address history
`Health data brokers` (IMS Health, IQVIA) - aggregate prescription and health app data, often without clear consent

sections.label: Stop feeding new data to brokers

items.name: Reduce the data you generate going forward
items.path: Applies across devices, apps, and accounts
items.why: Data brokers continuously refresh their databases. If you opt out of Spokeo today but don't change what data you're generating, your profile will repopulate within months. Reducing your data footprint upstream means fewer opt-outs to repeat.

steps.text: Disable location tracking on apps that don't need it - location data from apps is one of the primary sources brokers use
Opt out of third-party data sharing on every social media account and website - look in privacy settings for 'personalization,' 'data sharing,' or 'ad preferences'
Delete accounts on websites you no longer use - before deleting, request your data be removed from their database
Avoid using 'Sign in with Google / Facebook' on websites - these connections let the platform track which services you use
Use a pseudonym where possible when creating accounts on non-critical websites
Remove personal details from social media profiles - employer, hometown, phone number, relatives, relationship status
Opt out of prescreen credit offers at `optoutprescreen.com` - these generate a paper trail that brokers use

items.name: Manually opt out of data broker databases
items.why: Manual removal is free, thorough, and gives you direct control over what's removed. The downside is that it requires significant initial time and regular follow-up - brokers repopulate their databases continuously.

steps.text: Create a dedicated email address (ProtonMail recommended) solely for data broker opt-out communications - keep it separate from your primary inbox
Search your full name + city on Spokeo, BeenVerified, Whitepages, Intelius, PeopleFinder, TruthFinder, and Instant Checkmate. Screenshot what you find
Submit opt-out requests one by one. The Big Ass Data Broker Opt-Out List on GitHub has direct links to every broker's opt-out page
Keep a spreadsheet of which brokers you've submitted to, the date, and whether you received confirmation - many brokers take 30–45 days to process removals
Set a calendar reminder to repeat this process every 3–6 months - opt-outs are not permanent

items.name: Consider a paid data removal service
items.why: Paid services handle re-submissions automatically and provide regular reporting. The tradeoff is an ongoing subscription cost and they typically won't cover every broker. Best for people who want meaningful reduction without significant ongoing effort.

steps.text: `DeleteMe` (~$129/year) - one of the most established services, covers 750+ brokers with quarterly reports
`Incogni` (~$78/year, from Surfshark) - covers 180+ brokers with automated re-removal and a real-time dashboard
`EasyOptOuts` (~$20/year) - budget-friendly, more DIY but walks you through opt-outs systematically
`Optery` - free tier shows your exposure score; paid tiers handle automated removals across 200+ brokers
`Kanary` (~$99/year) - monitors and removes across 500+ sites, sends alerts when your data reappears

items.name: Opt out of people-finder and background check sites
items.why: People-finder sites expose your information to anyone willing to pay a few dollars - or sometimes for free. Anyone can look up your home address, previous addresses, phone number, email, and relatives. This data is used by stalkers, doxxers, scammers, and law enforcement agencies.

steps.text: `whitepages.com/suppression_requests` - Whitepages is one of the most widely used and feeds many other sites
`spokeo.com/optout` - search your name first, copy the URL of your profile, then paste it into the opt-out form
`beenverified.com/opt-out` - requires email verification to complete the opt-out
`intelius.com/opt-out` - part of the PeopleConnect family, which also includes Truthfinder and Instant Checkmate
`peoplefinder.com/optout.php` - straightforward form-based opt-out
For a comprehensive list of 200+ broker opt-out links, use the Big Ass Data Broker Opt-Out List on GitHub

items.name: Audit your public search footprint
items.why: Even if a broker removes your profile from their site, it may remain indexed in Google search results for months. Google has a removal tool for personal information that lets you request deindexing of pages containing your home address, phone number, or other sensitive data.

steps.text: Search `"[your full name]" "[your city]"` in quotes on Google, DuckDuckGo, and Bing. Note every site that surfaces your address or phone number
Also search `"[your full name]" "[your street address]"` to find specific address exposures
For each result that exposes personal information, visit `google.com/remove` and submit a removal request under 'Personal info in Google Search'
Google's removal tool covers: home addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, login credentials, and bank account numbers appearing in search results
Repeat this search every 3 months - broker sites get re-indexed even after removal

items.name: Build a removal maintenance schedule
items.why: Brokers source data from public records, credit bureaus, social media, and data purchases on a continuous basis. A profile you removed in January may reappear by July. The frequency at which your data reappears depends on how actively you're generating new data.

steps.text: Month 1: complete your first full round of opt-outs using the Big Ass Data Broker Opt-Out List. Set up your tracking spreadsheet and create your dedicated opt-out email
Month 2: confirm removals have been processed. Re-submit to any brokers that didn't respond or didn't remove your data
Every 3–6 months: repeat the Google self-search and re-submit opt-outs to the highest-priority people-finder sites
Annually: do a complete pass through your tracking spreadsheet, add any new brokers that have appeared, and delete any accounts you're no longer using

items.name: Essential removal resources
items.why: Using established community-maintained resources saves significant time during your initial opt-out sweep and ensures you're working from up-to-date information.

steps.text: `github.com/yaelwrites` - Big Ass Data Broker Opt-Out List. The most comprehensive community-maintained list of broker opt-out links (200+)
`inteltechniques.com` - IntelTechniques Data Removal Workbook. Free PDF walking through removal for major brokers
`privacyguides.org` - community-reviewed guides covering removal strategies and services
`google.com/remove` - request removal of your personal info from Google Search results
`optoutprescreen.com` - official FTC-backed tool to opt out of prescreen credit and insurance offers
`haveibeenpwned.com` - check if your email address has appeared in known data breaches
